despite two quarters of contraction, the recession remained limited, while GDP was forecast to fall 0.2% in 2023.","question_ids":["5B.9","6B.6","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The measures and outcomes occurred or were forecast during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the measures to the German federal government; electricity and gas price relief measures supported consumption but did not fully offset the decline.","question_ids":["5B.9","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Observed first-quarter 2023 result.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the relief measures to the federal government; it does not identify Scholz's personal decision-making role.","limitations":["The finding concerns national outcomes and does not isolate the chancellor's contribution."]},{"source_id":"SRC-35379f09c0b89cda","start_unit":65,"end_unit":66,"fact_summary":"DIW estimated that the federal government's energy-crisis relief packages and economic stabilization shield totaled about €279.2 billion for packages I–III and €195.3 billion for the shield; the measures supported private consumption by 2.3 percentage points in the first year.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.9","6B.1","6B.6","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Programs were enacted from 2022 and remained operative in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the packages and shield to the German federal government; no personal attribution to Scholz is provided.","limitations":["The estimate is model-based and covers multi-year measures, not only 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-35379f09c0b89cda","start_unit":66,"end_unit":66,"fact_summary":"DIW found that social transfers, energy-consumption transfers, and gas-market stabilization supported consumption among lower-income households more than among higher-income households, while tax relief favored higher-income households somewhat more.","question_ids":["5B.8","6B.3","6B.8","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Distributional effects were modeled for the 2023 energy-crisis measures.","ruler_attribution":"The source evaluates federal-government measures; it does not establish Scholz's individual authorship.","limitations":["These are simulated distributional effects rather than observed long-term incidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-35379f09c0b89cda","start_unit":72,"end_unit":77,"fact_summary":"The 2023 federal fiscal package included higher child benefit, Bürgergeld, expanded housing support, hospital and care-facility assistance, support for Ukrainian refugees, energy price brakes, and increased defense spending; DIW estimated the overall measures were mildly expansionary at 0.3% of GDP.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Measures and fiscal effects are reported for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes these budgetary measures to the federal government, without separately attributing them to Scholz.","limitations":["The source does not assess implementation quality for each program."]},{"source_id":"SRC-35379f09c0b89cda","start_unit":78,"end_unit":78,"fact_summary":"DIW estimated that 2023 fiscal measures raised household income by 0.76% of GDP, with lower-income households receiving about 0.2% of GDP in relief and higher-income groups about 0.5%;
